statement: The supplied source text genuinely contains no derivation of the particle filter (such as via importance weight derivation, marginalization, or recursive substitution); rather, it directly defines a particle filter (sequential Monte Carlo method) as a genetic-type Monte Carlo algorithm approximating the posterior distributions of a Markov process in a nonlinear state-space system using empirical particle measures. Specifically, the filtering distribution at step k is defined and approximated by \widehat{p}(dx_k|y_0,\dots,y_k) := \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \delta_{\widehat{\xi}_k^i}(dx_k) \approx \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{p(y_k|\xi_k^i)}{\sum_{j=1}^N p(y_k|\xi_k^j)} \delta_{\xi_k^i}(dx_k), evolving sequentially via selection-updating transitions \xi_k \mapsto \widehat{\xi}_k sampled with common distribution \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{p(y_k|\xi_k^i)}{\sum_{j=1}^N p(y_k|\xi_k^j)} \delta_{\xi_k^i}(dx_k) and mutation-prediction transitions \widehat{\xi}_k \mapsto \xi_{k+1} sampled independently as \xi_{k+1}^i \sim p(x_{k+1}|\widehat{\xi}_k^i).

symbols.meaning: internal state of the Markov process at time step k
i-th particle prior to selection (prediction particle) at time step k
i-th selected/updated particle at time step k
Dirac measure concentrated at state a
likelihood function of observation y_k evaluated at state x_k
conditional state transition probability density from x_k to x_{k+1}
empirical particle approximation of the filtering posterior distribution

mapping operator from the set of probability distributions into itself

properties.property: Approximation of filtering expectations for bounded test functions
properties.why: The empirical measure converges as N \to \infty, allowing expectations of bounded functions f under the posterior to be approximated by particle averages with bounded Monte Carlo error.

properties.property: Approximation of path-space joint distributions via ancestral lines
properties.why: Tracking ancestral lines (\widehat{\xi}_{0,k}^i, \dots, \widehat{\xi}_{k,k}^i) yields an empirical measure that approximates the full trajectory posterior p(d(x_0,\dots,x_k)|y_0,\dots,y_k) as N \to \infty.

The nonlinear filtering evolution is expressed as a dynamical system \eta_{n+1} = \Phi_{n+1}(\eta_n) approximated by sampling conditionally independent particles from \Phi_{n+1}(\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \delta_{\xi_n^i}).
The selection-updating transition resamples particles with weights proportional to the observation likelihood p(y_k|\xi_k^i).

assumptions.breaks_when: All particles evaluate to zero observation likelihood p(y_k|\xi_k^i) = 0, causing division by zero in proportional selection weights.

assumptions.assumption: Markov process dynamics and partial/noisy observation structure
assumptions.breaks_when: State dynamics have unmodeled history dependence not captured by the Markov transition density p(x_{k+1}|x_k).

failure_modes.signature: Poor approximation accuracy and sample degeneracy
failure_modes.cause: Particle filtering methods do not perform well when applied to very high-dimensional systems.

failure_modes.signature: Undefined selection probabilities due to zero denominator
failure_modes.cause: Observation y_k falls completely outside the support of the predicted particle cloud \xi_k^i.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so particle_filter is recorded as a definition
